title: A waltz, four ways of breathing
work: Waltz in C-sharp minor, Op. 64 No. 2
question: How do four pianists distribute time between the singing opening and the revolving continuation?
intro: Paderewski’s 1917 transfer, Pachmann’s 1925 HMV side and Rummel’s 1943 recording are compared with Olga Gurevich’s modern Musopen performance. Pachmann’s original file contains Étude Op. 25 No. 3 first, so only the waltz beginning around 1:57 is aligned. Paderewski’s automatic map is usable only with caution, while Rummel is limited to the shared opening because the later full-file path becomes unreliable. These restrictions preserve the original audio rather than inventing a continuous correspondence across every second.

recordings.label: Paderewski, 1917
recordings.note: Automatic alignment requires caution; compare broad phrases, not note-exact delays or a global tempo ratio.

recordings.label: Vladimir de Pachmann, 1925
recordings.note: Waltz starts around 1:57 after Étude Op. 25 No. 3 on the original side; pre-waltz material is outside the comparison.

recordings.label: Walter Morse Rummel, 1943
recordings.note: Shared opening only; later full-file correspondence failed inspection. Use the unedited recording without extrapolating the map.

recordings.label: Olga Gurevich, c. 2014
recordings.note: Modern reference; high-level regions recur rather than building continuously towards the end.

passages.label: Opening waltz
passages.note: Compare the length and shape of the singing phrase. Historic recording balance is not a direct measure of piano touch.

passages.label: An early turn
passages.note: A measured reference change lies within the shared opening of all four files; automatic correspondence remains provisional.

passages.label: Quicker figure
passages.note: Follow the revolving motion through the contrast. Rummel’s published map does not extend to the complete later return structure.

passages.label: Early recorded crest
passages.note: Gurevich’s highest five-second level window occurs here; compare phrase placement rather than normalised amplitude across different recordings.

passages.label: Central contrast
passages.note: Rummel is outside its published map here. The other files remain available, with Paderewski’s lower-confidence correspondence clearly cautioned.

passages.label: Later renewed span
passages.note: Compare the later phrase with the opening while retaining the distinction between a source-file duration and musical time.

alignment.scope: Pachmann: only source 117–276. Rummel: reference 0–76 to source 0–82.5. Paderewski is cautious, not a note-exact alignment.
alignment.method: Automatic chroma CENS + DTW; no audio speed change or concatenation.
